cycles.name: Bedrock
focuses: Rebuild the whole programme around home kit, with the upper back still leading and every session inside 45 minutes.
Set your home baselines: two filmed test sets and a logged number on every exercise, so Cycle 2 is built on real data instead of gym numbers that no longer apply.

paragraphs: Same block, new gym. Everything in here now runs in your flat with the kit you've got, and honestly a few things get better. Your legs were doing about 28kg a side on that leg press. One leg at a time with your own bodyweight is more than double that, so the work goes up, not down.

The job hasn't changed. Your upper back is still the main target, and you'll pull about three times more than you push. What has changed is that you now own bands, and your gym never had any. The shoulder blade work I wanted for you all along is finally possible.

Effort stays at 7 out of 10. You've got ten days left in this block and two things I want measured at the end of it, so treat these days as setting your starting line. Cycle 2 gets built off what you log here.
outcomes: Every session logged with a number in the box
Back stays quiet through the whole block
Both test sets filmed and sent
A daily walk, not just on training days
Real home numbers to build Cycle 2 from

cycles.name: Rigging
focuses: Hypertrophy-bias upper back and posterior chain — rows, pulls, rear delts — the engine of the tone and posture goal.
The hinge graduates: light dumbbell RDL grooved at RPE 7 or under while the hip thrust still carries the load.

paragraphs: Cycle 2 is called Rigging, and the name fits your flat better than it ever fit a gym. Ropes, straps and bands, all aimed at the one thing you asked me to fix.
This block finds your starting numbers. The next one pushes them.
Show me ten quiet days and we go hunting.

cycles.name: Keystone
focuses: First real strength push — barbell RDL enters at conservative loads, squat and press build toward RPE 8 top sets.
Upper-back volume held as the standing posture floor; the week gets a sharper load identity — one peak, one moderate, one low day.

cycles.name: Rebuild & Reset
focuses: Planned back-off — volume down roughly 40%, every RPE capped at 7, more movement variety so it reads as a new program, not a punishment.
Posture consolidation and an honest check-in on sleep and stress before the heaviest block is allowed to start.

cycles.name: Ironworks
focuses: The heaviest block of the roadmap — top-set and back-off work on squat, hinge and press at RPE 7–8.
Accessories cut to the minimum effective dose so the recovery budget goes to the bar.

cycles.name: Silhouette
focuses: Hypertrophy finishing block biased to upper back, shoulders and arms — the visible shape payoff.
Strength held on low-dose heavy anchors; closes with a posture re-check and the next-arc decision.

cards.title: Your gym is your flat now
cards.body:
Everything in here has been rebuilt around what you actually own. No machines, no cables, no barbell. Your bodyweight, some bands, the TRX and those dumbbells. This is not a downgrade. A single-leg squat at your bodyweight is heavier work than the leg press you were doing.

Five days now, like you asked. Day 1 is pull, Day 2 is legs and hinge, Day 3 is press and shoulder blades, Day 4 is legs again, Day 5 is a short posture and core day, about twenty minutes.

Three rules on the week, and these matter more than hitting five:

  • Never do Day 2 and Day 4 back to back. Leave a full day between them.
  • Four hard sessions in any seven days, maximum. Day 5 doesn't count, it's light.
  • If a day falls apart, the first main exercise on its own still counts as a session. Do that and log it.

Easiest way to run it: Day 1, Day 2, Day 5, rest, Day 3, Day 4, rest, then Day 1 and Day 2 again. You don't have to follow that, but it works.

cards.title: Your back, now that I'm not there
cards.body:
Your back was quiet through all four sessions last block, including a 60kg squat you put on yourself. That's genuinely good news and it's why you've got a real hinge in this program. But you're training on your own now, so read this properly.

Normal and fine: muscle burn, being tired, feeling stiff the next morning. Keep training through all of it.

Not fine: sharp pain, anything shooting down your leg, numbness or pins and needles, or pain that builds through a set instead of staying flat.

  • Mild and it fades, finish the set and write it in your log.
  • Building up, or it changes how you move, stop that exercise, use the swap on the card, message me.
  • Sharp, shooting, numb or just feels wrong, stop the session and message me before the next one.

One more, specific to the pull through. Finish every rep with your glutes, and stop when your hips are straight. Don't lean back past straight. The band pulls hardest right at the top and that's where a tired back takes over.

cards.title: Twenty minutes before you start
cards.body:
Do this once, before your first session. It'll save you the whole block.

  • Pick one door for the TRX and the bands. It has to open away from you. Close it, lock it, put a note on the other side.
  • Test it. Lean back on the TRX at the easiest angle and hold ten seconds. If the door or the anchor moves at all, stop and message me.
  • Tape six marks on your floor for the TRX rows, closest to furthest.
  • Number your bands 1 to 5 with a marker, lightest to heaviest.
  • Measure your step and push it hard on one edge to check it doesn't tip.
  • Measure the surfaces you'll use for push-ups. They have to be solid and against a wall. Not a chair, not a table that slides.

Then send me photos of all of it, plus one of how your pull-up bar is fixed to the wall. Nothing hangs off that bar this block, not you and not a band, until I've seen how it's mounted.

cards.title: There are no kilos at home
cards.body:
Most of this program has no weight on it, so the weight box gets a different number. Same box, same habit, just a different thing going in it.

  • TRX rows and hamstring curls: your floor mark number, 1 to 6.
  • Anything with a band: your band number, 1 to 5.
  • Push-ups: the height of your hands in cm.
  • Dumbbell work: kilos, like always. Put 0 when it's bodyweight.
  • Planks and holds: seconds.

You already did this yourself last block when you wrote the pin marks on the pulldown, so you know how it works. Log a number every single set. Without it I'm coaching you blind, and at home I can't see anything else.

cards.title: Effort, when there's no weight to add
cards.body:
Almost everything here is new to you, so week one is you finding your settings. On a new movement, start easier than you think. Do the first set, ask yourself how hard that was out of 10. A 5 means go harder next set. An 8 or 9 means back off.

Going harder at home means changing your leverage, not adding weight. Walk your feet closer on the TRX. Lower your hands on the push-up. Next band up. That's your weight stack now.

I have to say this one straight, because it happened last block. You hit a 10 out of 10 on the shoulder press when the card said 7. You're strong and you pick things up fast, and that's exactly what makes it easy to blow past the number. Seven means seven. There are two test sets at the end of this block and those are the only places you go all out.

And on a bad day, take 1 off every target. If it says 7, do 6. Anything already at 6 stays at 6.

cards.title: Film these two
cards.body:
Two exercises get tested at the end of this block, and both need to be on video. These are the numbers Cycle 2 gets built from, so they matter more than anything else you do in the next ten days.

  • TRX Row, as many clean reps as you can at one mark. Second time you run Day 1.
  • Split squat, as many clean reps as you can per leg, bodyweight. Second time you run Day 2.

Both stop at the first rep that slows down, gets shorter or loses position. Not the rep you fail on. These two are the only sets in the whole block where you're allowed past 7 out of 10.

Send me both. I'm not standing next to you any more, so film is how I coach you now. If the videos don't come, the numbers don't move.

cards.title: You already proved the thing that mattered
cards.body:
Look at your own dates. You trained four times in eight days. I asked for three a week. You beat it.

And your back stayed silent the whole way, through a 60kg squat you decided on yourself. That was the one question this block existed to answer, and you answered it. It's the reason you've got a real hinge in this program instead of me still tiptoeing around you.

You're also still holding the 9kg you lost. Keeping it off is harder than taking it off and most people don't manage it.

Then it stopped. I don't know why yet and I'm not guessing, so tell me what happened after the 9th. Whatever it was, it wasn't the training, because the training was working.

cards.title: The number I actually want to move
cards.body:
Your habit log says you're walking between 500 and 6,000 steps a day. That's the most fixable number in your whole file and it's costing you more than any exercise in here.

Thirty minutes of walking, every day, not just training days. It's written on Day 5 but I mean daily. Early morning or after sunset, it's August in Tehran and if you plan it for the afternoon you won't go.

One other thing. Your sleep is better than you told me at the start. You said 5 out of 10, but you've been logging 7 to 8 hours. That's a solid base and it's why I'm comfortable giving you five days instead of three.
